knownTrap_functionsNodeModules: 🛑 MEASURED 2026-10-18. Installing functions/node_modules (needed only to get tsup for `npm --prefix ./functions run build`) takes the Stop hook from 22 SECONDS to a 10-MINUTE TIMEOUT. Some audit walks functions/ without excluding node_modules; it is gitignored so nothing catches it. Workaround in place: the directory is renamed to functions/node_modules_parked. Rename it back to build the bundle, then park it again — or better, FIND the audit and add the exclusion, since the next person to run `npm install` in functions/ silently loses their whole audit gate. Candidates: any audit walking functions/ (ssr-in-appkit, use-client, catch-normalize all do directory walks).
knownTrap_interruptedToolCall: 🛑 A user message arriving mid-turn can interrupt a tool call that ALREADY PARTIALLY EXECUTED. Measured 2026-10-18: an append to appkit/src/server.ts landed, the turn was interrupted, and the next turn appended a SECOND copy — producing 'Duplicate identifier', which read as 'already done, the note was stale'. A git checkout then removed BOTH copies, so the follow-up grep reported every symbol missing. Three readings, each accurate when taken, pointing three different ways. After any interruption, re-establish state by COUNTING (grep -c) and by loading the built artifact — never by re-reading source and trusting the first answer.

trap_localDevPinOnMain: 🛑 MAIN IS NOW IN LOCAL-DEV MODE. package.json pins `@mohasinac/appkit: file:./appkit` and tsconfig.json includes the two appkit/src lines. Both came in with the merge and are CORRECT for continued development — but both MUST be reverted before any Vercel deploy: a `file:` pin breaks `npm ci` on Vercel (dist is gitignored, so the link resolves to a dist-less directory), and appkit/src in the consumer tsconfig causes a Linux OOM/case-sensitivity failure after 5-8 minutes with no accessible error log (Root Cause #23). scripts/deploy.mjs pre-flights both, so use it rather than a bare `vercel --prod`.
trap_pipeMasksExitStatus: 🛑 `cmd | tail` makes the PIPE's exit status the chain's, so `git checkout X 2>&1 | tail -1 && git commit ...` RUNS THE COMMIT even when the checkout failed. Measured 2026-10-18: a branch already checked out in another worktree refused the switch, the chain continued, and the commit landed on detached HEAD — then main fast-forwarded past it. Recovered via reflog (ede05aa2 -> cherry-pick c870c809), nothing lost. The same bug produced an earlier false 'NOT FF' answer that was reported to the user before being caught: a failed `cd` short-circuited into the || branch. Never pipe a git command whose exit status gates the next one, and never trust a bare echo in a || branch as a measurement.
open_stopHookSlow_UNDIAGNOSED: 🛑 INTERMITTENT AND UNDIAGNOSED. check-on-stop usually runs 21-25s and has twice hung past 10 MINUTES. I recorded TWO confident causes and BOTH were wrong: (1) functions/node_modules being installed — disproven, main has it present and runs in 21s; (2) my node_modules_parked workaround not matching functions/.gitignore — disproven, it hung in main where no parked dir exists, then ran clean 25s later with nothing changed. hint_rasteriserCanBeVerifiedWITHOUTEyes: Useful for the next session: the rasteriser does NOT need visual inspection to be verified, which is what makes it safe to land in one sitting. Rasterise KNOWN shapes and check the filled area numerically — (1) an axis-aligned square of side n must fill exactly n*n; (2) a circle of radius r approximated by the standard four cubics (control offset 0.5523*r) must fill pi*r^2 within ~1% if coverage anti-aliasing works, and will come out visibly low or high with a broken fill rule; (3) a path traced clockwise and the same path reversed must fill IDENTICALLY — that is the real test of the fill rule, and the one a hand-written scanline loop usually fails. Then one real part through the probe for a sanity look.
standing_dockerForLiveTuning:
🛑 LIVE TUNING RUNS GO THROUGH `npm run dev:docker` (user instruction, 2026-10-19), not `dev` or `dev:hot`. Measured in cgroup accounting: next start serves at 546 MB steady and does not grow, where the Turbopack dev server's arena grows with routes-visited-per-process and is invisible to --max-old-space-size. Live tuning visits the tracer page repeatedly, which is that growth's worst case.

KEEPING IT WARM — what does and does not cost a cold build:
  ✓ `dev:docker:stop` then `dev:docker` is WARM. The cache is a NAMED docker volume (letitrip-build-probe-cache, shared with probe-build-docker.mjs on purpose), so it survives container stop/start.
  ✗ `dev:docker -- --cold` discards the volume. Never pass it unless you intend ~5 minutes.
  ✗ `docker volume rm letitrip-build-probe-cache`, or a Docker Desktop factory reset / prune.

MEASURED: cold ~8,100 MB peak / 256-323s · warm 4,424 MB / 126s. The Docker VM holds 7,646 MB, so a COLD build does NOT fit in RAM and swaps — that is why cold is 2.5x the wall time rather than 2x the memory. Warm fits comfortably.

✓ THE HISTORIC COLD TRIGGER NO LONGER APPLIES. CLAUDE.md says an appkit VERSION BUMP forces a cold build because it invalidates node_modules and discards the cache. Main is now pinned `file:./appkit`, and the workflow is `npm --prefix appkit run build` + `node scripts/sync-appkit.mjs`, which overlays dist WITHOUT touching the dependency tree — so appkit changes no longer cost a cold rebuild. That is a real side benefit of moving off the registry pin, and it reverses on the next publish.
